text:
sam: quick q after the FA RFC — when we pick FlashAttention v2 vs v3 at runtime, what heuristics should drive it?

jess: +1. FAv3 seems promising but has some larger workspace requirements. do we prefer it always for long seqs?

dmitri: short answer: not always. FAv3 wins for long sequences and BF16/FP16 packed heads, but v2 still better in some tiny-head cases and where we need minimal workspace.

sam: can you elaborate on the thresholds? concrete numbers help for kernel selector.

jess: from our perf runs:
```
seq=128, head_dim=64, bsz=8: FAv2 ~ 6.2ms, FAv3 ~ 7.0ms, Triton ~ 9.4ms
seq=1024, head_dim=64, bsz=1: FAv2 ~ 85ms, FAv3 ~ 47ms, cuBLAS fallback ~ 210ms
seq=2048, head_dim=64, bsz=1: FAv3 wins by ~2-3x vs v2
```
(perf-bot)

perf-bot: posted full run @ s3://redwood-perf/flashattn/176900/ — metric breakdown per head_dim, dtype, batch, seq.

mike: important caveat re: workspace allocation. FAv3 needs transient workspace sized ~O(head_dim*seq) in some code paths. if we naively allocate per-request we get fragmentation and OOMs.

dmitri: agreed. proposal: workspace pool keyed by (device, dtype, head_dim_bucket, seq_bucket) with eviction after idle time. also use a conservative allocator for private deployments.

sam: what are head_dim_bucket and seq_bucket? how coarse should buckets be?

jess: empirical buckets that balance reuse vs waste. e.g., head_dim_bucket = [32,64,96,128,192,256+] ; seq_bucket = [<=128, <=512, <=1024, <=2048, >2048]. we round up requests to bucket sizes when selecting workspace.

dmitri: also add a fast-path: if request exactly matches an owned workspace, skip reallocation. this is critical for high QPS.

mike: fallback behavior: if FAv3 workspace allocation fails, we fall back to FAv2 if compatible, else to Triton/cuBLAS path. we should track the fallback counters in console.

jess: note FAv2 doesn't support certain fused qkv layouts we use on torchscript models — we need a small wrapper that reshapes/titles inputs before invoking FAv2. otherwise we force an expensive copy.

sam: interface question: does kernel selector live in serving runtime or in model adapter layer?

dmitri: runtime. reason: selector needs access to device memory state, pool stats, and global SLAs (latency vs cost). adapters expose model properties (num_heads, head_dim, dtype) and runtime chooses kernel.

jess: recommend API: KernelSelector.choose(model_signature, request_profile) -> KernelDecision string plus workspace_size hint. request_profile includes seq_len, batch, latency_budget_ms.

sam: and rollout strategy? want to test FAv3 in prod gradually.

perf-bot: experiment results: canary population (10% traffic) with FAv3 for seq>512 reduced tokens/sec cost by 28% for a doc-summarization workload, p95 latency unchanged within 1.5ms on dedicated pool.

dmitri: good. for canary we should add runtime toggle + automatic rollback if p95 increases by >5% or error rate spikes.

mike: operational flags: device-level disable for FAv3 when driver/kernel incompat issues arise. infra-bot can annotate device health and auto-disable on repeated CUDA kernel failures.

jess: QA note: FAv3's deterministic seeding and deterministic softmax handling differ slightly; we saw tiny numerical diffs in logits (~1e-4) that were ok for most workloads but broke a few eval tests. include a "strict-numeric" flag which forces v2/canonical path.

sam: perf vs quality tradeoff seems manageable. any memory-safety edge cases?

dmitri: watch out for very wide heads (head_dim >= 384) where FAv3 currently allocates very large workspace. we may cap and force chunked attention. document that in model onboarding.

jess: also need improved logs: KernelDecision logs must include why v3/v2 selected (reason tags: seq_bucket, head_bucket, latency_priority, fallback_count). small logs otherwise too opaque.

mike: rollout TODOs:
- add metric for workspace pool hit-rate
- per-model kernel selection overrides for customers on Dedicated
- infra knob to set bucket thresholds globally

sam: timeline? can we land selector + pool + canary in two sprints?

dmitri: sprint 1: kernel selector + basic pool + metrics. sprint 2: per-model overrides + canary orchestration + strict-numeric flag.

jess: I'll sketch KernelSelector interface and add perf thresholds to RFC followup doc. @dmitri will you add workspace pool design?

dmitri: yes. I'll add a short state machine for fallback logic.

sam: great. thanks everyone. I'll annotate the RFC with these action items. :thumbsup:
